title: Mistakes by group
prompt:
One overall score can hide trouble. Write `error_rate(rows)`, the share of tickets the model got wrong, and `rates_by_group(rows)`, which gives each group its own error rate.

The twelve tickets are fictional. When it works, `python3 rates.py` shows that phone bookings get far more wrong answers than online bookings.
expected_output:
all: 33% wrong
online: 12% wrong
phone: 75% wrong
hints: Count the rows where `real != guess`, then divide by `len(rows)`.
For groups, first sort the rows into lists: `groups.setdefault(group, []).append(row)`.
Then build the answer with one `error_rate` call per group: `{g: error_rate(rows) for g, rows in groups.items()}`.
explain_after: Jurafsky and Martin warn that machine learning systems can replicate and even amplify the biases in their training data [ml-100]. Splitting a score by group is one simple way to look for that. Here the online bookings get 1 of 8 wrong and the phone bookings 3 of 4; the overall number alone would hide the gap.
